page.layout: One block of verse in four stanzas, set in the centre of the page. Running head at the top centre. Catchword at the lower right.

l.i: Post longa exilia & laqueos cinerésque suorum;
Quos inter pietate grauis venerandus honora
Canicie, dextram medios qui lætus in ignes
Coniecit, nostro fulget memorabilis ævo
Crammerus; pete culta, Liber, quæ Sequana lambit,
Quæ Ligeris secat & Rhodanus, rapidúsque Garunna.
I, Liber, & veteres mœrens invise tot urbes
Quà Rhenus fluit: auriferis quà dives arenis
Turbidus Oceanum leni Tagus agmine pulsat:
Et te Roma legat caput imperiúmque malorum.
Tu vero tu CHRISTE fave, cursúmque secunda,
Cælestíque patrocinio mendacia contra
Et vulgi rabiem, præsens monimenta tuorum
Incisa his tabulis iam ter rediviva tucre,
Queis latè circùm tua lux & gloria crescant.
Hæc ego, dum dulces licet intermittere curas,
Montibus in nostris cælo sub teste canebam.
Quo ter felicem me tempore chara tenebat
Hieropolis, ducente Deo, purgata nefandis
Monstrorum tot conciliis, tectáque suorum
Invidia; instantes lachrymans dum plango ruinas
Labentis patriæ, luctúsque & fata meorum:
Et dum quisque bonus, penitus rerum ordine verso,
Omnia iam pessum ruere infelice ruina
Conqueritur, Puerique adeo, lachrymabile Regnum.

page.notes: The Greek-style ampersand (&) is kept as printed. Capitalised names (Liber, Sequana, Rhodanus, Garunna, Roma, Tagus, CHRISTE, Hieropolis, Regnum) may be set in roman type in the print; I have rendered the whole verse as italic. The catchword ADMO- is printed with its hyphen. No page number is printed on this page. The word "cinerésque" and the accents on "latè", "circùm" and "imperiúmque" are read from the scan and should be checked against the original.
